title: enMotion 800-Ft Rolls vs. Scott Pro 1,150-Ft Hard Roll Towels: Commercial Dispenser & Cost-Per-Dry Comparison
seoTitle: enMotion 800-Ft vs. Scott Pro 1,150-Ft Hard Roll Towels Compared
metaDescription: enMotion 800-ft vs. Scott Pro 1,150-ft hard roll towels compared by core lock, dry-hand yield, and $0.012-$0.025/sq ft supply math in our calculator.
excerpt: Georgia-Pacific enMotion 800-foot rolls and Kimberly-Clark Scott Pro 1,150-foot hard rolls dominate US commercial office restrooms, but their proprietary cores, roll widths, and sheet densities serve different facility priorities. Here is how facility managers compare dry-hand yield, restock intervals, and companion restroom hardware.
quickAnswer: Choose Georgia-Pacific enMotion 800-foot roll systems (including the compact 8-inch enMotion Impulse dispenser) when executive touchless presentation, whisper-quiet operation, and single-sheet through-air-dried absorbency are top priorities; choose Scott Pro 1,150-foot compressed hard rolls (1.75-inch blue/purple core) when maximizing linear footage between custodian visits in high-headcount restrooms is paramount. Direct-purchasing either system outperforms the standard $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit janitorial contractor consumables markup.

blocks.text: The Head-to-Head Showdown in US Commercial Restrooms

Walk into any Class A corporate office tower, medical office suite, or multi-tenant commercial building in the United States, and you are almost guaranteed to encounter one of two proprietary roll towel ecosystems: Georgia-Pacific's enMotion platform (anchored by 800-foot 10-inch rolls or 700-to-800-foot 8-inch Impulse rolls) or Kimberly-Clark Professional's Scott Pro High-Capacity Hard Roll system (engineered around compressed 1,150-foot 8-inch rolls). Both manufacturers utilize proprietary core plugs and internal dispenser mandrels to lock building owners into their respective paper refills.

For an office facility manager overseeing a 10,000 to 24,999 sq ft floorplate ($0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft base cleaning rate) or a 2,500 to 9,999 sq ft suite ($0.09 to $0.15 per sq ft), choosing between enMotion 800-foot rolls and Scott Pro 1,150-foot hard rolls requires looking past raw linear footage on the shipping carton. An 800-foot roll that dries a pair of wet hands with a single 10-inch sheet can deliver a lower cost-per-dry than a 1,150-foot roll if employees feel compelled to pull two 12-inch sheets from a thinner web.

blocks.title: Why Linear Footage Alone Misleads Facility Buyers
blocks.text: A 6-roll case of enMotion 800-foot rolls provides 4,800 linear feet per case, while a 6-roll case of Scott Pro 1,150-foot hard rolls provides 6,900 linear feet per case—a 43.7% raw footage advantage for Scott Pro. However, 10-inch enMotion rolls are 25% wider (10 inches vs. 8 inches), meaning a 6-roll case of 10-inch enMotion paper actually contains 4,000 square feet of towel surface area compared to 4,600 square feet in a 6-roll case of 8-inch Scott Pro 1,150-foot rolls—closing the real surface-area gap to just 15%.
Engineering Breakdown: enMotion 800-Ft vs. Scott Pro 1,150-Ft

Before standardizing your restroom and breakroom walls, compare how these two industry heavyweights handle core architecture, absorbency pockets, cabinet footprint, and custodian labor across 4.33 weeks per month:

items: Core & Mandrel Geometry: enMotion rolls use grooved plastic end plugs that snap into Georgia-Pacific's precision tension arms on both the 10-inch automated chassis and the Georgia-Pacific enMotion Impulse 8-Inch Compact Towel Dispenser. Scott Pro 1,150-foot rolls use a color-coded 1.75-inch slotted core engineered exclusively for Scott Pro electronic and mechanical dispensers. Neither roll is cross-compatible without changing the wall cabinet.

Fiber Loft & Absorbency Technology: enMotion rolls prioritize plush fabric-like hand feel and rapid water wicking for executive suites, client-facing law or financial offices, and medical clinics. Scott Pro 1,150-foot rolls utilize Kimberly-Clark's Absorbency Pockets technology in a tighter, high-compression wind so that 350 extra linear feet fit inside the same outer roll diameter.

Cabinet Footprint for Tight Walls & Breakrooms: When wall width or under-cabinet clearance is restricted, the Georgia-Pacific enMotion Impulse 8-Inch Compact Towel Dispenser scales the touchless enMotion platform down to an 8-inch roll format powered by 4 D-cell batteries, making it ideal for single-occupant restrooms and office kitchenettes.

Janitorial Service Interval Matching: In offices cleaned twice weekly (8.66 visits per month, 1.00 frequency multiplier) or three times weekly (13.0 visits per month, 0.95 multiplier), high-headcount restrooms with only one towel dispenser benefit from Scott Pro's 1,150-foot roll length to prevent Friday afternoon run-outs. In daily-cleaned offices (5x-week at 21.65 visits per month, 0.90 multiplier), an 800-foot enMotion roll easily spans multiple days with superior guest impression.

blocks.text: Building a Touchless, Zero-Run-Out Restroom Ecosystem

Whether you standardize your multi-stall restrooms on 800-foot enMotion rolls or 1,150-foot Scott Pro rolls, your satellite sinks and single-occupant executive restrooms need hardware that shares the same low-maintenance philosophy. The Georgia-Pacific enMotion Impulse 8-Inch Compact Towel Dispenser delivers the exact same touchless infrared hygiene and programmable sheet-length control as the full-size 10-inch enMotion unit in a slim, compact housing powered by 4 standard D-cell batteries. It mounts easily above boutique restroom vanities or inside office kitchenettes without crowding mirrors or backsplash tiles.

Next, address the two consumables that run out alongside hand towels: toilet tissue and hand soap. Installing the Georgia-Pacific Compact Vertical Coreless Toilet Paper Dispenser replaces bulky 9-inch jumbo tissue shrouds with a sleek vertical dual-roll cabinet that holds up to 3,000 sheets of 2-ply coreless bath tissue. Because there is no cardboard inner core and an automatic drop-down transfer mechanism, 100% of every roll is used before the janitor replaces it. At the sink vanity, specify PURELL ES8 1200 mL Healthy Soap Foam Refill (2-Pack)—a fragrance-free, dye-free green-certified foam formulation with a factory-sealed nozzle that eliminates the mold and bacterial biofilm hazards found in open bulk-pour liquid soap reservoirs.

Finally, streamline your evening janitorial waste collection ($35 to $65 per hour standard labor across ceramic tile-and-grout restroom floors at a 1.12x multiplier) by pairing two purpose-built commercial liners. Line your 44-gallon janitor Brute barrels and high-volume restroom receptacles with Boardwalk 40x48 High-Density 45-Gallon Commercial Trash Liners (250-Case), featuring a 16-micron star-seal base that conforms smoothly to round or square containers without leaking damp hand-towel moisture. For hallway and copy-room recycling bins, use Plasticplace 30x36 Clear 20–30 Gallon Recycling Can Liners (250-Case), whose clear 0.75-mil LLDPE film lets custodians verify at a glance that no wet food or restroom paper waste has contaminated the recycling stream.
How to Transition Between Proprietary Roll Towel Platforms

items.text: Pull the past 90 days of paper invoices or contractor consumables charges ($0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit) and calculate your actual linear feet consumed per 100 building occupants across 4.33 weeks per month.

items.name: Match Dispenser Footprint to Tile Anchors Before Swapping
items.text: When replacing legacy cabinets over ceramic tile walls, check whether the new enMotion Impulse 8-inch or 10-inch chassis backplate covers existing drill holes so you avoid costly tile patching or stainless wall-plate retrofits.

items.name: Standardize Battery & Refill PM Schedules
items.text: Instruct your janitorial crew lead to replace the 4 D-cell alkaline batteries in electronic roll dispensers every 12 months (or every 80 to 100 rolls) during a scheduled quarterly deep-cleaning visit.

items.name: Sync Soap and Coreless Tissue Restock Thresholds
items.text: Pair each 800-foot to 1,150-foot towel roll change with a visual check of the PURELL ES8 1200 mL foam soap refill and Georgia-Pacific Compact Vertical Coreless tissue spindle so no restroom triggers a mid-day facility ticket.

faqs.q: Will Scott Pro 1,150-ft hard rolls fit inside a Georgia-Pacific enMotion dispenser?
faqs.a: No. Georgia-Pacific enMotion dispensers (both the 10-inch full-size and the 8-inch enMotion Impulse) use proprietary grooved core plugs and specific roll-width sensor arms, while Scott Pro 1,150-foot rolls use Kimberly-Clark's proprietary 1.75-inch slotted blue or purple core plug. Attempting to force a non-compatible roll into either dispenser will jam the drive roller and void the hardware warranty.

faqs.q: Which roll towel system reduces janitorial labor more in a 15,000 sq ft office cleaned 3 times per week?
faqs.a: In a 15,000 sq ft office cleaned 3 times weekly (13.0 visits per month at 4.33 weeks per month, base rate $0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft), both systems perform exceptionally well, but Scott Pro's 1,150-foot roll holds 43% more linear feet per spool than an 800-foot roll. If your main restroom has only a single wall dispenser serving 60+ employees, the 1,150-foot length provides extra insurance against running empty over the 72-hour weekend gap between Friday and Monday night cleanings.

faqs.q: Why do commercial janitorial contracts recommend sealed 1,200 mL foam soap cartridges like PURELL ES8 over bulk-pour soap?
faqs.a: Peer-reviewed environmental hygiene studies and CDC hand-hygiene guidance warn that open refillable bulk-pour soap dispensers develop bacterial biofilm inside the permanent pump nozzle when topped off repeatedly. Sealed cartridges like the PURELL ES8 1200 mL Healthy Soap Foam Refill include a fresh factory-sealed dosing pump on every refill and meet OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200) labeling standards without exposing janitors to messy liquid transfers.

faqs.q: How do clear 30x36 liners help our office avoid municipal commercial recycling fines?
faqs.a: Many US municipalities and commercial waste haulers levy contamination surcharges if restroom paper towels or food waste are mixed into single-stream office recycling dumpsters. Using Plasticplace 30x36 Clear 0.75-mil LLDPE liners in copy rooms and recycling stations while restricting opaque or high-density Boardwalk 40x48 16-micron liners to restroom and general trash Brute barrels prevents night crews from accidentally dumping wet restroom towels into the recycling bale.
